# Getting Started

RECAP captures experimental provenance through resources, process templates,
and process runs. Start with the local workflow, then use the remote workflow
when a RECAP server owns the database.

## Find the right documentation

RECAP documentation is organized around four complementary ways to use the
documentation:

- **Getting Started** provides guided lessons for learning RECAP by doing. Begin
  with [Complete Provenance Workflow](04-complete-provenance-workflow.qmd), then
  use the shorter [Quick Start: Create and Store Data Locally](../how-to/quick-start-create-and-store-data-locally.qmd)
  when you need a task recipe.
- **How-To Guides** provide focused procedures for users who need to complete a
  specific task. Use [How-To Guides](../how-to/index.qmd) for templates,
  servers, queries, authentication, and provenance operations.
- **Explanation** describes how RECAP works and why its architecture matters.
  Read [Explanation](../explanation/index.qmd) when you need concepts before
  choosing an implementation approach.
- **Tutorials** show complete domain workflows from setup through working code.
  Browse [Tutorials](../tutorials/index.qmd) when you want a guided path.
- **Reference** lists generated public APIs, schemas, query families, and
  builder methods. Browse [API Reference](/reference/index.html) for exact
  signatures and model fields.

## Choose a workflow

- [Quick start: create and store data locally](../how-to/quick-start-create-and-store-data-locally.qmd)
  with SQLite.
- [Use a remote RECAP server](../how-to/setup-recap-server.qmd) with REST query/read and
  command transports. Requests use ordinary JSON; local and remote QueryDSL,
  canonical identity, and load-aware models remain aligned.
